evidence: The original code validated every token before the help/version check, so `--help --nope` errored while `--help --force --force-no backup` printed help, an inconsistency the agent confirms. Fix f12ecc6 returns from Parse the moment help/version is consumed, which keeps `-c --help list` reading --help as the config-file value; tests pin all three cases.

The agent quotes the spec as "Options may appear before the subcommand", which grants permission and prohibits nothing, and notes that the usage lines are docopt patterns, where `[options]` matches in any position. Rejecting `mackup backup --force` would narrow the grammar. The reviewer's 'override the intended action' harm does not exist because options only set run modes.
guidance_note: When the implementation deliberately accepts a broader grammar than the usage lines spell out, say so in the usage text in the original PR; this pushback left that gap and F8 re-raised the same point.

evidence: The agent quotes appspec/02: "No subcommand (`mackup` with no positional command): prints the usage block; observed exit `0`". The spec's discriminator is the absence of a positional command, not an empty argv, so `mackup --verbose` falls in that clause. The packet holds only the agent's quotation of the spec, but the quotation is specific and was not contested.

The reviewer named a closed pipe as the example, and SIGPIPE does cover that case on fd 1/2. The underlying claim, that write failures are discarded and Main exits 0, is still true for a redirect to a full disk (ENOSPC). The agent conceded this in F9: "I under-addressed it last round ... exits 0 with truncated output".
guidance_note: When rebutting a silent-failure finding by naming the mechanism that handles the reviewer's example, list every way that write can fail (EPIPE, ENOSPC, EIO, a failing fake writer) and check whether the mechanism covers each one before pushing back.

evidence: Go module versions always carry a leading v, so the build-info path would have printed `Mackup v0.11.1`. In f12ecc6 the fix routes both the stamped value and the build-info value through `normalize`, and tests cover the stamped, normalized, and fallback paths.
guidance_note: When a value comes from an external format (Go module versions), check its documented shape against the spec's output contract before writing the passthrough.

evidence: The stub carries `TODO(macklebox-resolvers-5iw.2)`, and the agent quotes the ticket as requiring "the config-load step stubbed until the resolvers epic lands". Every dispatch arm exits non-zero with 'not implemented', so no stub can reach a success exit, and the reviewer asked for resolver work that belongs to other tickets.

A bare invocation (CmdNone) also returns ExitOK without loading config, so the "only paths" claim was false. f12ecc6 deletes that sentence from app.go. The same sentence remained in app_test.go, and F10 found it.
guidance_note: When deleting a false claim from a comment, grep the repo for the same phrase (here "only paths") and fix every copy in the same commit.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive. This is F2 raised again against parse.go code that f12ecc6 did not change; f12ecc6 only added the help/version early return. The agent kept the parser behavior, which was correct for the reasons given on F2, and accepted the real kernel: the usage text never said where options may go. 448b6d3 adds "Options may be given before or after the subcommand."
guidance_note: When pushing back on a grammar finding because the code deliberately accepts more than the usage text shows, update the usage text in the same reply so the next round has nothing to re-raise.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive. f12ecc6 did not touch io.go; this is F4 raised again after the agent wrongly pushed back, and it adds the ENOSPC case. In 448b6d3, IO records the first write error and Main checks it once, which delivers the reviewer's non-zero-exit guarantee without returning an error from every print helper.
guidance_note: Close a silent-failure finding in the first round with the cheapest sound mechanism (record the first write error, check it where the exit code is decided) instead of pushing back and paying for a re-raise.

evidence: The app_test.go comment "appspec/02: they are the only paths that succeed while skipping the..." repeats the claim F7 removed from app.go. The agent admits: "I fixed this sentence in `app.go` last round and left the copy of it here." The flagged commit 448b6d3 did not add this comment; it is the copy F7's fix missed.
guidance_note: When a finding says a claim is false, search for the claim's wording across code, tests, and docs before naming the fix commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. 448b6d3 did not touch dispatch.go or stages.go, so the shared TODO IDs predate review. The agent quotes 5iw.4's description, which covers both list/show and the usable-environment check, so splitting the IDs would invent a ticket. The real ambiguity was the bare `// TODO(<id>)` lines, and 7d85a2e fixed it by adding what each seam waits for.
guidance_note: Write every TODO with what the seam is waiting for alongside the ticket id, so the id is never the only thing linking two seams.

evidence: 448b6d3 (the F9 fix) guarded both the diagnostic and the downgrade with `err != nil && code == ExitOK`, which withheld the write-failure diagnostic from runs that were already failing. Only the diagnostic half of the finding is real, since a failing run already returns a failure code. 7d85a2e moved the diagnostic outside the guard and kept the downgrade guarded.
guidance_note: When adding a check that gates two separate effects (report the error, change the exit code), decide the condition for each effect separately rather than putting both under one guard.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. The `--` endOfOpts branch and TestParseDoubleDashEndsOptions already existed when f12ecc6 was reviewed, and 448b6d3 did not touch parse.go. The agent confirmed that appspec/02 never mentions `--` and that no catalog key starts with a dash, so removing it in 7d85a2e removed invented grammar.
guidance_note: Before adding parser syntax the spec does not list (such as a `--` sentinel), confirm the spec or catalog needs it; in the original PR it was speculative generality.

evidence: The agent shows a transcript: `make clean` leaves no bin/, then `make build` exits 0 and produces bin/mackup, because `go build -o` creates the parent directory. The flag is a false positive because 448b6d3 did not touch the Makefile.

The early return inside the short-cluster loop (`if inv.Opts.Help || inv.Opts.Version { return inv, nil }`) was added by f12ecc6, the F1 fix, so this finding is on code that fix created. The behavior is the rule F1 established applied consistently: `-hz` is the same as `-h -z`, and help stops the scan. The finding exposes no defect, so it cost a thread but not an avoidable bug.

narrative: This PR bootstraps the mackup argv parser, startup pipeline, and stream wrappers. The agent made mostly sound calls, including well-evidenced pushbacks on F2, F3, F6, and F14. The one wrong call was the F4 pushback, which relied on SIGPIPE covering every write failure; the reviewer re-raised it as F9, and the F9 fix itself had an over-wide guard that F12 caught. F7's comment deletion missed a copy of the same sentence in app_test.go, which became F10. Every round would have run anyway because each push triggers a review and round 2 also found real pre-existing issues (F11, F13), so no full round was avoidable, but three findings across rounds 1 and 2 came from incomplete earlier handling.
guidance_observations: When pushing back, check the rebuttal against every case covered by the reviewer's general claim, not only the example the reviewer gave; F4 was argued from the closed-pipe example alone.
A deliberately broader behavior that is pushed back on should be stated in user-facing text in the same round (F2 → F8); otherwise the reviewer re-raises it.
Fixing a false sentence should include a repo-wide search for duplicates of it (F7 → F10).
The agent's citations of the spec and ticket text were specific and quoted, which made its pushbacks checkable.
